Drive through one and your toy pops into a different toy in the middle of the run, keeping its speed: the grippy Stomper monster truck climbs anything, the Pinewood racer is fast but slippery, the Tubtug boat floats and paddles across the bath, the Zoomrod rocket car burns fuel to fly over gaps, the heavy Scoopy digger shoves blocks out of the way, and the Boingo spring buggy charges up and hops. Reading each course and timing every swap is the puzzle.

There are 100 hand-built levels in ten worlds, from the Playroom Rug to the dark Attic Toy Chest, each with three stars that are explained before you start: reach the flag, beat the par time, and grab the gold sticker that hides off the fast line. Stars and coins unlock new worlds, paints for every toy, drivers and finish-line effects on the Toy Shelf. The Daily Toy Box gives everyone the same new course each day with two or three swaps, and keeps your day streak.

Crashes are part of the fun: every crash plays back instantly in slow motion, and you can retry in under a second or share the crash as a flipbook card. Finish a level and you see where you stand, with your rank, percentile and the next rank to beat, then send a challenge link so a friend races your exact ghost, verified by replaying it on their device. Everything works offline, progress is saved on your device, and leaderboard numbers are marked as preview until online ranks launch.

how.d: Hold GAS to drive and BRAKE to brake or reverse. In the air, GAS tips your toy back and BRAKE tips it forward.
Drive through a swap gate and your toy becomes a monster truck, racer, boat, rocket car, digger or spring buggy, keeping its speed.
Reach the flag, beat the par time and grab the gold sticker on each of 100 levels in ten toy-box worlds.
The Daily Toy Box is the same new course for everyone each day. Share a link so a friend races your ghost.

about: Multiplatoon is a crowd-runner where your times tables are your weapon. You lead a squad of painted tin toy soldiers down a cardboard road laid across a bedroom floor, and every few steps the road splits into two cellophane gates propped up on pencils. Each gate shows a little sum: "4×6" adds twenty-four soldiers, "×2" doubles the whole squad, a red "−3×5" takes fifteen away and "÷2" halves you. Work out which side gives more, slide into it with one thumb and watch the platoon swell or shrink. A pop-up shows the worked fact ("4 × 6 = 24") every time, so the tables sink in while you play.

Further along, rival squads with spiky helmets block the road and clash with your soldiers one for one, spinning tops sweep across one side of the road, and at the end a cardboard castle waits with its own garrison. Bring a big enough army to topple it. There are fifteen levels across three worlds (Bedroom Floor, Playroom Rug and Attic at Night), each built around one times table from the 2s to the 12s, mixing in earlier tables as you go. Every level has three stars, shown on a goal card before you start, tracked live on screen and explained on the results screen: topple the castle, reach the target army size, and pick the bigger gate every time. The results screen also lists the facts you marched through.

The Daily March is a new seeded course every day, the same for everyone, with a streak to keep, and Endless March keeps building castles until your army runs out. Medals earned from stars and soldiers buy a bigger starting squad in the Barracks, and you can unlock eight uniforms, from Garden Guard green to Golden Parade. After every run you see your global rank, your percentile and the next army size to beat. If you are playing offline it is a clearly labelled preview against sample players. Share a picture card that reads "My army hit 2,048" or a challenge link that drops a friend into the same course with your army to beat. Progress, stars, medals and streaks are saved on your device. It plays in portrait or landscape with one thumb, a mouse or the arrow keys, and works offline.

how.d: Drag left or right anywhere with one thumb, hold and drag with a mouse, or use the arrow keys or A and D.
Each gate shows a times-table sum. Work out which side gives more soldiers and steer into it; the worked fact pops up every time.
Clash with rival squads, dodge spinning tops and bring a big enough army to topple the castle at the end of each level.
The Daily March is the same new course for everyone each day, and Endless March keeps building castles until your army runs out.

about: Morphmaw.io is an eat-to-evolve monster brawler drawn as glossy die-cut stickers on doodled notebook pages. You start as Blip, a tiny one-eyed blob. Gobble the snacks scattered across the page to fill your DNA bar, bite monsters smaller than you, and run from the big ones. Every monster wears a coloured ring: green means prey, yellow means an even fight, red means run. Red arrows at the edge of the screen warn you when something hungry is closing in, and bushes let you hide.

When your DNA bar is full you curl up in a safe cocoon and choose your next form from two or three cards. There are three lineages and 34 forms in all. Chomp monsters lunge forward with a big bite, Spike monsters spin and hit everything around them, and Puff monsters spit slowing globs from range. You can stay in your line or branch into a neighbouring one, so every run grows into a different creature, from Nibbit and Prickle to the form-12 apex beasts. Reaching form 12 earns a special share card.

Six arenas (Margin Meadow, Sticky Desk, Crayon Canyon, Blueprint Bay, Eraser Peaks and Sketchbook Summit) each have a goal card and three stars: reach a target form, knock out a number of monsters in one run, and climb to number one on the food chain. Earning a star opens the next page. The Daily Arena gives everyone the same map and a twist such as Snack Storm or Giant Day, and keeps your streak. The Evolution Codex records every form you discover, and stars, KOs and discoveries unlock sticker finishes like Glitter, Holo Shine and Gold Foil.

After each run you see the stars you earned and missed, your DNA score, a clearly labelled preview of your global standing, and a share card with your evolution path plus a challenge link that loads the same arena and rivals for a friend. Rivals are offline bots, so it plays anywhere with no account. Progress is saved in your browser on this device.

how.d: Drag anywhere with one thumb, steer with the mouse pointer, or use WASD or the arrow keys.
Gobble snacks and bite monsters with a green ring. Yellow is an even fight, red means run.
When the DNA bar is full, pick your next form from the cards: Chomp, Spike or Puff.
Each arena has three stars on its goal card. The Daily Arena is the same map for everyone each day.

keys: Touch: drag to move, tap BITE

about: Daubstorm is a bright, family-friendly paint arena game. You are a little ink drop with a blaster full of colour, and your team has one minute to cover more of the arena than the other side. Nothing gets hurt: a rival who takes too much paint just goes splat, pops back at base and jumps straight back into the fight.

Every match is 2 against 2. You and your buddy bot face two rivals across a hand-drawn arena of hedges, crates, piers and ice. Paint the floor in your colour and refill your ink by standing in your own paint. Fill the storm meter to unleash a Daubstorm, a huge burst that soaks the ground around you. A live bar shows the score for both teams, and a mini-map shows who owns which corner.

There are 24 levels across four seasons: Petal Park in spring, Sunny Pier in summer, Leafy Yard in autumn and Frosty Rink in winter. Rivals get smarter as you go, and every sixth level is a longer boss match. Each level has three stars, and each star says why: win the match, reach a team-paint goal, or hit a personal target such as splats, paint share or a Daubstorm. The goal card shows all three before you start, the HUD tracks them live, and the results card explains which you earned.

A new Daily Arena arrives every day with a seeded map and blaster that are the same for everyone on that date. Play daily to grow your streak. Stars unlock new blasters (Spray Fan, Lobber and Roller), hats for your drop and new paint colours in the Locker.

Share a colourful result card with a challenge link. It opens the same arena for a friend and shows your score as the one to beat. Play with twin touch sticks, mouse and keyboard, or Apple Pencil, in portrait or landscape. Turn on Auto-paint to have the game aim and fire for you while you steer. Progress is saved on your device, and the game works offline.

how.d: Touch: the left side of the screen moves, the right side aims and paints. Desktop: WASD or arrows move, the mouse aims and click paints.
Team up with your buddy bot and paint more of the arena than the rival team before the 60 seconds run out.
Fill the storm meter and unleash a Daubstorm. Tap AUTO to turn on auto-aim and auto-paint.
Each level has three stars with clear goals. The Daily Daub is the same arena for everyone each day.

keys: WASD + mouse to aim and paint

about: Gulpopolis is a two-minute race to become the biggest hole in town. You are a little round hole with a hungry rim, and the whole city is on the menu. Drag anywhere to steer (or just move the mouse) and glide over anything smaller than you: cones, hydrants, people on the sidewalk, ducks in the park pond, benches and bikes. Every bite makes you wider, and every new size opens a new tier of food. Soon you are slurping parasols and trees, then cars and taxis, buses and trucks, then whole houses, cafés and shops, office blocks, the downtown towers and, if you are quick, the Spire and the Stadium itself.

You are not alone. Five rival holes with names like Munchkin, Big Burp and Chompette are racing you for the same city. Bump into a smaller hole and you gulp it whole; meet a much bigger one and run. A live mini board shows who is ahead, arrows at the edge of the screen point to nearby rivals, pink for danger and teal for prey, and the last thirty seconds turn the music up for a frantic finish.

Every round has three clear stars: finish on the podium, reach Size 8, and chain a 60-gulp combo. Swallows that follow each other quickly build a combo that multiplies your points, with a pop, a wobble and a rising gulp for every bite. After the round you see the final standings, how close you came, the stars you earned and missed, and where your score would rank. Coins from each round buy upgrades (a bigger start, more speed, stronger suction) and new rim skins.

There is a Daily City that is the same for every player, with a streak to keep, and a share card with a beat-me link that drops your friend into your exact city with your score to beat. Until online leaderboards launch, global ranks are an offline preview against a generated field of sample players, and the game always says so.
Progress saves automatically on your device. Gulpopolis plays in portrait or landscape on phones, tablets and desktop, with touch, mouse or keyboard, and a restart takes under a second.

how.d: Drag anywhere to steer (a joystick appears under your finger), let the hole follow your mouse, or use WASD or the arrow keys.
Anything smaller than your hole falls in. Gulp lots in a row for a combo and grow big enough for houses, towers and the stadium.
Five rival holes race you for two minutes. Swallow a smaller rival, and steer clear of bigger ones.
Each round has three stars on its goal card. Coins buy skins and upgrades, and the Daily City is the same map for everyone each day.

keys: Mouse: the hole follows the pointer

about: Sizzle & Mizzle is a two-spirit puzzle platformer set inside a glowing temple of stained glass. Sizzle is a little ember who strolls across lava but fizzles out in water; Mizzle is a drop of mist who wades through water but boils away in lava. Gloom pools swallow anyone. Bring both spirits to their own doors to clear a level.

The twist is that their powers combine. Sizzle's flare lights braziers, melts ice and bakes wet clay into solid brick, and it boils a water pool into a rising column of steam that lifts anyone standing on it. Mizzle's splash fills fonts, freezes water into an ice bridge that Sizzle can cross (if he does not stand still too long), and soaks dusty walls into mud you can climb through. Pressure plates, levers, gates, lifts and crates tie the two routes together, so every level is a small conversation between fire and water.

There are 40 hand-made levels in four chapters: the Ember Nave, the Rain Cloister, the Kiln Crypt and the Rose Spire. Every level was proven solvable by an automated solver in both its normal and mirrored form. Each level has three clearly explained stars (finish, collect every gem, beat the par time) and a speed rank from S to C. A goal card shows the stars before you start, the HUD tracks gems and time, and the results card explains what you earned and what you missed. The game never moves on by itself and a restart is instant.

Play alone or together. On a phone one player steers one spirit at a time and taps the swap button to switch. On an iPad two friends share the screen with split controls, one on each side. On a computer two players share the keyboard: A, D, W and S for Sizzle, the arrow keys for Mizzle.

Every day brings a Daily mirror: one level, flipped, the same for everyone, with a streak to keep. After every clear you see your global standing and percentile (currently from a clearly labelled offline preview board), and you can share a duo time card or send a beat-my-time challenge link that opens the same level for a friend. Earn stars, S ranks and daily streaks to unlock new looks for both spirits. Progress, best times and cosmetics are saved on your device automatically. All art, music and sound are generated in the game, with nothing downloaded.

how.d: Sizzle the fire spirit walks on lava but fizzles in water. Mizzle the mist spirit wades through water but boils in lava. Gloom pools stop both.
Sizzle's flare lights braziers, melts ice and boils water into steam lifts. Mizzle's splash fills fonts, freezes water into bridges and soaks walls into mud.
Alone, tap the swap button to switch spirits. On an iPad two friends share split controls; on a computer Sizzle uses A D W S and Mizzle the arrow keys.
Bring both spirits to their doors. Each level has three stars and a speed rank, and the Daily Mirror is one flipped level, the same for everyone each day.

keys: Sizzle: A D W, flare S
Phone: swap button · iPad: split controls

about: Origarrison is a merge tower defense game made of cut paper. A line of paper critters is marching along a strip of kraft tape towards your little paper keep, and the only thing in their way is whatever you can fold in time.

Tap Fold to spend ink and a fresh tier-1 tower pops onto a free spot beside the path. Fold two of the same kind and drag one onto the other: they merge into a stronger tower with a satisfying crinkle, a flash and a rising chime. Twin tier-2s make a tier 3, and so on all the way to a glittering tier-8 prism tower. Every critter you fold back into scrap pays ink, so a good merge now buys the next fold sooner.

Four tower families each have a job. Cranes throw darts and are the only early answer to flying kites. Frogs hop onto the path and splash whole groups, and they crush the armoured box critters that darts bounce off. Fans blow a gust that slows everything in front of them, and Stars chain a spark from one critter to the next. Quick darts, slow armoured boxes, kites that fly straight over the path and an origami boss every ten waves keep you mixing families and moving towers around. Drag a tower to any free spot to reposition it, swap two towers, or drop one in the bin to sell it for ink.

Each desk has three stars to earn: survive wave 10, fold a tier-5 tower, and survive wave 20. Stars unlock new desks with new paths, reaching new waves unlocks new tower families, and coins buy paper skins such as Newsprint, Washi and Foil. Call the next wave early for bonus ink, or turn on double speed when you feel confident. The Daily Fold gives every player the same desk, seed and twist for the day, with a streak to keep. After every run you see your best wave, your stars, the next unlock and where you would stand on the leaderboard. Until online leaderboards launch, that standing is an offline preview against sample players, and the game always says so.

Share a card of your run with a challenge link that drops a friend onto your exact desk with your wave to beat. Progress saves automatically on your device. Origarrison plays in portrait or landscape on phones, tablets and desktop, with touch, mouse or keyboard.

how.d: Tap Fold to spend ink on a new tier-1 tower. Drag a tower onto an identical twin to merge it into the next tier, all the way up to tier 8.
Cranes hit flying kites, Frogs splash groups and crush armoured boxes, Fans slow everything down and Stars chain sparks between critters.
Critters march along the tape to your paper keep. Drag towers to move or swap them, drop one in the bin to sell it, and call waves early for bonus ink.
Each desk has three stars: wave 10, a tier-5 tower and wave 20. The Daily Fold is one desk, seed and twist, the same for everyone each day.

keys: Touch or mouse: drag twin onto twin
F or Space folds, N next wave
X double speed, 1-4 picks a family

about: Moatball is a pinball tower defense game. Your castle gate sits at the bottom of a pinball table, a moat runs across the middle, and waves of wind-up critters are marching down the table to tear the gate. You have one steel ball, two flippers and whatever you can build between waves.

Between waves you pick parts from three cards and drop them into sockets on the table. Pop Bumpers kick the ball hard and shake nearby critters. Slingshots fire the ball back supercharged. Spinners throw darts as the ball passes, and Rampart Posts make critters walk the long way round. Later you unlock Magnets that bend the ball and slow critters, Zappers that chain lightning, Kick Saucers that catch the ball and fire it at the toughest target, and Splitters that add a second ball for a few seconds. Every part levels up the more the ball hits it, so where you put it matters as much as what you buy.

Then you start the wave and play pinball. The whole game works with one finger: touch and hold anywhere to raise both flippers, let go to drop them. Smash several critters in a row to build a combo up to x8 with a hit-stop crunch and a popup. Drain the ball and you lose the combo and half a heart from the gate. Six kinds of critter keep you changing your build: quick dashers, armoured shellbacks the ball must hit hard, flutters that fly over posts, splitbugs that burst into minis and shield bearers you must hit from behind. Every tenth wave brings a boss: the Tin Tortoise, the Ram Engine and the Clockwork Colossus.

Each wave lasts about a minute or two and has three stars: clear it, clear it without a leak, and clear it without a leak while reaching a x4 combo. Spend coins on boosts such as Gate Repair, Heavy Ball and Ball Saver, and spend gears earned from every run in the Workshop on permanent upgrades. Survive 30 waves to beat the table, then keep going in endless mode. The Daily Table gives every player the same seed and twist for the day, such as Rush Hour, Twin Balls or Thrift Shop, with a streak to keep.

After every run you see your best wave, your stars, the next unlock and where you would stand on the leaderboard. Until online leaderboards launch, that standing is an offline preview against sample players, and the game always says so. Share a card of your run with a challenge link that puts a friend on your exact table with your wave to beat. Progress saves automatically on your device. Moatball plays in portrait or landscape on phones, tablets and desktop, with touch, mouse or keyboard, and screen shake can be turned off in Settings.

how.d: Pick a part from three cards and drop it into a socket: Pop Bumpers, Slingshots, Spinners and Rampart Posts, then Magnets, Zappers, Kick Saucers and Splitters as you unlock them.
Touch and hold anywhere to raise both flippers, let go to drop them. One finger plays the whole game; on a computer use Space, the arrow keys, Z or X.
Hit critters in a row for a combo up to x8. A drained ball costs your combo and half a heart from the castle gate, and every tenth wave brings a boss.
Each wave has three stars: hold the gate, no leaks, and no leaks with a x4 combo. The Daily Table is one seed and twist, the same for everyone each day.

keys: Space, arrows, Z or X · N next wave

about: Whirlwatch is a tower defense game where the towers move. A sleepy little moon floats in the middle of the screen, wrapped in two rings of turret slots, and swarms of space critters drift in from every direction. Every turret only fires in front of it, so the real trick is aiming: drag anywhere to spin the inner ring and the outer ring turns the other way, geared like clockwork. Swing the right towers to face each wave before it arrives.

Build with stardust that the critters drop. Pebblers fire quick twin pellets, Frostbloom sprays icy mist that slows everything in its arc, Comet Mortar lobs splashing comets that crack armored Shellbacks, Arc Coil chains lightning between neighbours, Sunlance burns a long beam straight through armor, Gustbell blows whole groups back out, and Seeker Pods launch homing rockets in every direction. Tap two matching turrets to merge them into a stronger tier, up to tier III, or sell one to change your plan mid-wave.

The campaign has 40 levels across four star systems, from Pebble Reach and Ember Drift to Frostfall Belt and the Void Crown. Each system brings new critters, from speedy Darts and splitting Splitters to Swirlsnails that spiral as they come, Menders that heal their friends, blinking Phaselings and Broodmothers that hatch mites. Every tenth level ends in a boss: the Gloomwhale, the Ringcrawler, the Ember Twins and finally the Eclipse Maw with its orbiting shield moons. Warning arrows at the screen edge show where each wave will come from, so you always get a moment to turn.

Every level has three star goals shown before you start, during play and on the results card, such as losing almost no shield, building a tier II turret or finishing with stardust in the bank. Stars and level clears earn moonstones for the Moon Lab, where permanent upgrades add moon shield, starting stardust, turret damage, bigger bounties, better sell prices and a Prism Core that zaps critters that get too close.

The Daily Orbit is a new endless run every day with the same seed and the same three turret types for every player, so scores are comparable. Keep a daily streak, see how your score ranks, share a picture card of your rings, or send a challenge link that dares a friend to beat your score. The score travels inside the link, so nothing is uploaded.

Progress saves automatically on your device. Whirlwatch plays offline in portrait or landscape on phones, tablets and desktop, and every action works with one finger. Optional ads can revive you once in a level or double the moonstones from a level; they are never required.

how.d: Tap a glowing slot on a ring, then a turret card, and pay with stardust. Pebblers come first; Frostbloom, Comet Mortar, Arc Coil, Sunlance, Gustbell and Seeker Pods unlock as you go.
Every turret only fires in front of it. Drag anywhere to spin the rings (the outer ring turns the other way) and face the critters. Warning arrows show where each wave comes from.
Tap a turret, then a glowing twin of the same type and tier, to merge them into a stronger turret, up to tier III. Sell to change your plan mid-wave.

how.t: Stars, Moon Lab and Daily Orbit.
how.d: Each level has three star goals. Stars and clears earn moonstones for permanent Moon Lab upgrades. The Daily Orbit is the same endless run for everyone each day.

keys: Touch or mouse: drag to spin, tap to build
← → or A/D spin, 1-7 build, R merge
Enter launches, F speed, Esc pause

about: Yesterlings is a tower defense game with a time-loop twist: you do not build towers, you become them. Murklings creep down three lanes toward the Hearthlight, the little lantern that keeps the dusk away. You walk your hero around the field with one finger and fight whatever comes close. When the wave ends, your run turns into a Yesterling, a chalk-glow copy of you that replays every step you took and fights beside you in the next wave.

So every wave is two things at once: a fight you have to win now and a recording you will lean on later. Hold the left lane this wave and it is guarded for the rest of the level. Sweep the middle and your echo sweeps it again. Up to six Yesterlings play together, and when three or more of you hit the same foe at once you trigger a Chorus, a burst of light that hurts everything nearby, earns Glimmers and adds a note to the music, which grows a layer for every echo on the field.

Between waves you see the next wave's forecast and spend Glimmers on your shelf of echoes. Keep one so it never fades, Polish it to make it stronger, light a Beacon so echoes nearby swing faster, or Retake one you are not happy with. Eight kinds of foe keep you thinking: quick Skitters, armoured Puffshells, Driftwings that hop lanes, Hushers that silence echoes, Splitlets that burst in two, hulking Lumberbulks and the Fogmother boss every fifth level.

Twenty levels across four regions, from Dusk Meadow to Starfall Steps, each with three stars: protect the Hearthlight, keep most of your hearts, and meet the level's own goal. Unlock four heroes as you go, Brightblade, Sparkbow, Frostbell and Mendlamp, each with its own reach and ability, and spend Lantern Oil from your stars on permanent upgrades and new lantern glows. The Daily Echo gives every player the same seeded level and twist each day, with a streak to keep.

After every level you see your stars, your score and where you would stand on the leaderboard. Until online leaderboards launch that standing is an offline preview against sample players, and the game always says so. Share a card of your run with a challenge link that puts a friend on your exact level and seed with your score to beat. Progress, including a run in the middle of a level, saves automatically on your device. Yesterlings plays in portrait or landscape on phones, tablets and desktop, with touch, mouse or keyboard.

how.d: Tap or drag where your hero should walk; you hit any Murkling that comes close. On a computer click where to walk, press 1-3 to head for a lane and Space for your ability. Keep the Murklings away from the Hearthlight at the end of the three lanes.

how.t: Your past waves fight with you.
how.d: When a wave ends, your run becomes a Yesterling: a glowing echo that replays every step you took beside you in the next waves. Up to six play together, and the oldest fades unless you Keep it.
Spend Glimmers on your echoes: Keep one so it never fades, Polish it to make it stronger, light a Beacon so echoes nearby swing faster, or Retake one you are not happy with.
When you and two or more echoes hit the same foe at once you trigger a Chorus. Each level has three stars, and the Daily Echo is one seeded level and twist, the same for everyone each day.

keys: Touch: tap or drag to walk, tap the ability button
1-3 head for a lane, Space ability, Enter starts the wave

about: Lobwhistle is rooftop tennis at a sunny seaside resort. Your fox runs to the ball on its own. You only swipe: direction aims the shot, length sets how deep and how hard it flies, and a curve in the swipe puts spin on the ball so it bends and kicks. Glowing tiles on the far court fill a Fever meter. Fill it and your next swipe is a Whistle Shot, a faster spiralling trick shot. Five courts change the bounce: Promenade plays true, Clay Terrace sits up and slows down, Frost Pier skids, the Boardwalk springs, and Whistle Point adds a cross-wind you can read on the windsock. Each animal rival has a signature serve. Win the game, string a long rally, and land tiles in a row to earn three stars. Each day Seaspray Serve, the Lighthouse Open, deals the same seeded three-rival ladder to every player, and your best score is kept on this device. Portrait and landscape both play with one finger, a mouse drag, or the keyboard.

how.d: Your fox runs to the ball by itself. Swipe up to hit: the direction aims, the length sets how deep and hard, and a curve adds spin. A short tap is a safe shot.
Land the ball on the glowing tiles on the far court. Six hits fill the Fever meter and your next swipe is a Whistle Shot, a fast spiralling trick shot.
Every court bounces differently, from the slow Clay Terrace to the skiddy Frost Pier and the windy Whistle Point. Each rival has a signature serve.
Win, string a long rally and land tiles in a row for three stars. The daily Seaspray Serve gives everyone the same three-rival ladder each day.

keys: Touch: swipe up to hit, curve for spin
Arrows pick a lane, hold Space to charge

about: Short Fuse is a browser 3D shooter set in a shipyard at dusk. Rogue robots have taken the yard and your bomb fuse is already lit — every robot you destroy buys you more time. Play the 6-mission campaign through to the Foreman finale, train on the range, or jump into solo waves on six maps with four difficulty tiers.

Gun drops come in rarities you stash and equip; the store and daily missions keep a run going. Four operators, six weapons, jeeps and tanks, and a short story intro. Touch, mouse and keyboard all work. Multiplayer and global boards stay off on Fytoon for now (solo and daily only). Teen and up: this is a shooting game.

how.d: WASD or left stick to move, mouse or right stick to look. On a phone, left thumb moves and right thumb aims; the gun fires on its own while you hold.
Click or tap to fire. Q or the blast button spends your charged blast. Space jumps, Shift dashes, V changes vehicle camera.
Walk up to a jeep or tank and enter it. Pick up gun drops, energy cells and mission objects in the yard.
Clear six story missions with star goals, or play the daily challenge that is the same seed for everyone that day.

keys: Mouse: look, click to fire, WASD move
Touch: left move, right aim; gun fires while held
Q blast, Space jump, Shift dash, V vehicle view

about: Bubbletoom is a seaside festival puzzle about one good shot. It is dusk on Gullhaven Pier, the lanterns are up, and a sky full of festival bubbles hangs over the tide pool. Drag to aim the lifebuoy launcher, let go to fire, and watch the dotted guide show exactly where the bubble will bank off the pier posts and where it will stick. Land it next to two or more of its own colour and they pop. Anything left hanging with nothing holding it up splashes into the sea, and those drops are worth far more than pops, so the real game is spotting the one bubble that brings a whole cluster down.

Every few shots the tide pushes a new row in from the top, and if the bubbles reach the rope you are out, so plan your banks before the board creeps down. Big pops and drops fill the Fever meter. When it is full your next shot is a rainbow Storm bubble that clears everything around where it lands. Chain scoring shots for a combo multiplier up to five times, and swap the spare bubble whenever the current colour does not fit.

Each of the 30 designed levels has three stars to earn: clear the board, land one big aimed mid-run shot that pops or drops a set number of bubbles (a Storm or the finishing shot does not count), and finish without wasting more than a few shots. The goal card tells you the targets before you play, the HUD tracks them live, and the results screen shows what you earned and what you missed. Levels unlock as you clear them and never start on their own.

The Daily Regatta is one seeded board that is the same for every player that day, with a streak for every day you come back. After each run you see where your score stands, and you can share a picture of your result with a challenge link that opens the very same board with your score as the target to beat.

Every bubble carries its own symbol (shell, star, fish, heart, leaf or drop) so colour is never the only clue. Bubbletoom plays one-handed on a phone in portrait or landscape, with a mouse, or entirely from the keyboard, and your best scores, stars, unlocks and streak are saved on this device.

how.d: Drag and let go to fire the lifebuoy launcher, or hover and click. The dotted guide shows the exact path, including banks off the pier posts.
Land next to two or more of the same colour to pop them. Anything left hanging falls into the sea, and drops score far more than pops.
Every few shots a new row pushes in. Clear the board before the bubbles reach the rope. Fill the Fever meter for a rainbow Storm bubble.
30 levels with three stars each, plus a Daily Regatta board that is the same for everyone, with a streak and a challenge link to share.

keys: Touch: drag to aim, let go to fire, tap the spare bubble to swap
Mouse: hover or drag to aim, click to fire
Left/Right aim, Space fire, X swap
